summary: Medicare Advantage (Humana MA, Anthem MA, UHC MA, Wellcare; KY and IN). 1) Whether a plan must answer, and by when, turns first on whether the practice has a written contract with that MA plan/product. NON-CONTRACTED: hard federal clocks. Clean claims must be paid within 30 days of receipt (95% standard) with Prompt Payment Act interest from day 31 (Treasury rate 4.75% Jul-Dec 2026, 4.125% Jan-Jun 2026); every other claim must be paid or denied within 60 calendar days (42 CFR 422.520(a)). Silence past the deadline is itself an adverse organization determination that can be appealed (422.568(f)). The payment floor is what Original Medicare would pay (MPFS; 95% if the practice is Medicare non-par) (422.100(b)(2), 422.214, CMS). With a signed Waiver of Liability the practice is a party (422.574(b)) and can request reconsideration within 60 days of receipt of the notice (receipt presumed 5 days after the notice date, so 65 days) of any denial, partial payment, downcode, bundling edit or level-of-care reduction (CMS appeals guidance 50.1.1, effective July 6, 2026). The plan must decide and pay within 60 days or, if it upholds in any part or misses the clock, automatically send the file to the CMS Part C IRE (C2C Innovative Solutions since May 1, 2026), which decides payment cases within 60 days; after an IRE reversal the plan must pay within 30 days (422.590(b),(d); 422.618). Next come the ALJ ($200 in 2026 and 2027; claims can be aggregated), the Medicare Appeals Council and federal court ($1,960 in 2026; $2,000 in 2027). Late forwards and IRE overturns count against the plan's Star Ratings measures C30 and C31 (weight 2 each), and CMS's 2027 Technical Notes say these include appeals requested by non-contract providers. Dismissals are allowed only for the reasons in 422.582(f) (CMS calls the list exhaustive) and are reviewable by the IRE. CONTRACTED: since the April 2025 rule, a contracted provider's payment denial is not subject to the Subpart M appeal/IRE process when the member owes nothing more (422.562(c)(2)). The plan must pay under the contract's prompt-payment clause (422.520(b)), and timelines come from the contract and the plan's manual: Anthem MA reconsideration within 120 days of the EOP with a 45-day resolution target, then appeal within 30 days with a 30-day target; UHC 12 months for reconsideration plus appeal, then a Notice of Dispute within 60 days of the appeal decision or arbitration rights are waived, and a bulk Claims Research Project for 20+ same-issue claims; Humana disputes within 18 months; Wellcare provider appeals within 90 days with up to 60 days to decide. Federal rules still bind the plan's conduct toward contracted physicians: physician review with appropriate expertise before medical-necessity denials (422.566(d)); coverage limited to Medicare rules or publicly posted evidence-based internal criteria and decided on the individual patient's records, not a population algorithm (422.101(b)(6),(c); CMS FAQ of Feb. 6, 2024); no later medical-necessity denial after a PA/pre-service/concurrent approval (422.138(c)); a PA for a course of treatment (e.g., radiation) is valid as long as medically necessary, with a 90-day transition for new enrollees (422.112(b)(8)); PA decisions in 7 days (72 hours expedited) with a specific denial reason (422.568(b), 422.122(a)); and the treating physician's pre-service reconsiderations do go to the IRE. 2) Kentucky and Indiana prompt-pay statutes do not apply to MA plans: federal MA standards supersede state law other than licensing and solvency (42 U.S.C. 1395w-26(b)(3); 42 CFR 422.402); Humana's manual says the same. 3) The independent CMS Payment Dispute Resolution contractor no longer exists: CMS says it ran from 2009 until January 31, 2014; since then providers dispute directly with the plan and may complain through 1-800-MEDICARE, and CMS says its account managers monitor MA plans on non-contract payment disputes. No current Medicare Managed Care Manual chapter on a PDR process was found. 4) Complaint channels: CMS's online provider complaint form (live since Dec. 22, 2025) feeds the Complaints Tracking Module; plans must try to contact the filer within 7 days and resolve within 30 days of assignment (2 days immediate need, 7 urgent) (422.125). CTM complaint rates feed Star Ratings measure C27 (weight 2); the 2025 CTM SOP (seen only via a third-party copy) does not mark category 2.70 'Improper, insufficient, or delayed claims payment' as excluded, but also says CMS is not a party to contractual matters. Regional Offices: Atlanta (KY) ROATLORA@cms.hhs.gov; Chicago (IN) ROCHIORA@cms.hhs.gov. 5) Enforcement belongs to CMS: substantial failure on appeals or prompt payment is a listed ground for contract termination, intermediate sanctions and civil money penalties (422.510(a)(4)(ii),(v); 422.752; 422.760), and CMS may pay providers directly and cut the plan's payments (422.520(c); 42 U.S.C. 1395w-27(f)(2)). 6) Letters that hold up against an AI reviewer cite the exact rule, clock and consequence; state only true facts (contract status, WOL attached, receipt dates); never claim state prompt-pay interest, or IRE rights a contracted provider does not have; demand the specific Medicare rule or publicly posted criterion and the reviewer's field; and say plainly that silence is an adverse determination and that an uphold or late decision sends the file to the CMS IRE. Payer-manual conflicts to press: Humana's 2026 manual limits non-par appeals to full/zero-pay, medical-necessity and non-covered denials, and Anthem's guidebook limits non-par appeals to denials with member liability, while CMS guidance 50.1.1 gives non-contracted providers with a WOL full appeal rights for partial payments, downcoding and bundling; UHC's non-contracted sheet gives 60 days to appeal versus CMS's 60 days after presumed receipt (65 days).

rules.quote: (1) ... the MA organization will pay 95 percent of the “clean claims” within 30 days of receipt if they are ... claims for services that are not furnished under a written agreement between the organization and the provider. ... (3) All other claims from non-contracted providers must be paid or denied within 60 calendar days from the date of the request.
rules.applies_to: All MA plans (HMO, PPO, PFFS, MSA; Humana MA, Anthem MA, UHC MA, Wellcare MA) for services by a provider with NO written agreement with that MA organization for those services. Not contracted providers (see MA-03). Federal rule; applies in KY and IN regardless of state law.
rules.requires: Pay 95% of clean claims (no defect, no missing substantiating documentation, conforms to Original Medicare clean-claim rules per 422.500) within 30 days of receipt; pay or deny every other non-contracted claim within 60 calendar days of the request. 422.504(c): plan must comply with 422.520 'and with instructions issued by CMS'.
rules.deadline: Clean claim: 30 days from plan receipt. Any other non-contracted claim: paid or denied within 60 calendar days from the date of the request.
rules.consequence: Interest on late clean claims (MA-02). A claim not paid/denied in time is an adverse organization determination the provider can appeal (MA-05). 422.520(c): after notice and hearing CMS may pay providers directly and reduce the plan's payments. Substantial failure is a listed ground for contract termination (422.510(a)(4)(v)) and civil money penalties (MA-27).
rules.provider_use: Day-31 and day-61 chase letters: state the claim is from a non-contracted provider, give the receipt date (clearinghouse acceptance report), cite 422.520(a), demand payment with interest, and state that silence past day 60 is an adverse organization determination that the practice will appeal with a signed Waiver of Liability, which the plan must decide within 60 days or forward to the CMS IRE. Keep the 999/277CA acceptance proof for every claim so the clock can be proven in bulk.

rules.citation: 42 CFR 422.520(a)(2); 42 U.S.C. 1395u(c)(2)(B)-(C) (SSA 1842(c)(2)); 31 U.S.C. 3902(a) rate as published by Treasury; CMS Pub. 100-04 Ch.1 sec. 80.2.2 (FFS method)
rules.quote: 422.520(a)(2): “The MA organization must pay interest on clean claims that are not paid within 30 days in accordance with sections 1816(c)(2)(B) and 1842(c)(2)(B).” 42 U.S.C. 1395u(c)(2)(C): “interest shall be paid at the rate used for purposes of section 3902(a) of title 31 ... for the period beginning on the day after the required payment date and ending on the date on which payment is made.” Treasury: “The Prompt Payment interest rate for July 1– December 31, 2026 is 4.75%.”
rules.applies_to: MA plans paying clean claims of non-contracted providers (and PFFS enrollee claims). Not contracted providers unless their contract provides interest.
rules.requires: Pay simple interest on a clean claim paid after day 30, from day 31 to the payment date, at the Treasury Prompt Payment rate. Treasury table: Jul-Dec 2026 4.75%; Jan-Jun 2026 4.125%; Jul-Dec 2025 4.625%; Jan-Jun 2025 4.625%. FFS method (Pub. 100-04 80.2.2): payment x rate x days / 365, rate in effect on the day of payment, rounded to the penny.
rules.deadline: Interest accrues from the day after the 30th day following receipt of the clean claim until the day of payment.
rules.consequence: Unpaid interest is part of the amount owed under the CMS contract; CMS enforcement as in MA-01. Note: under the FFS manual, interest is not paid on full denials or on claims first denied and later paid on appeal; whether MA plans may apply those same exceptions is not stated in any MA source found.
rules.provider_use: Compute interest automatically on every late-paid non-contracted clean claim and add an interest line to the bulk demand (e.g., $100 paid 30 days late at 4.75% = $0.39). Cite 422.520(a)(2) and the statute; do not claim KY/IN statutory prompt-pay interest on MA claims (preempted, MA-04). Note: 422.520(a)(2) cites 1842(c)(2)(B), but in the current statute the interest sentence is subparagraph (C); quote the statute text, not just the letter.

rules.quote: 422.520(b)(1): “Contracts or other written agreements between MA organizations and providers must contain a prompt payment provision, the terms of which are developed and agreed to by both the MA organization and the relevant provider. (2) The MA organization is obligated to pay contracted providers under the terms of the contract between the MA organization and the provider.”
rules.applies_to: Contracted (participating) providers of MA plans. Payment timing and dispute rights come from the contract and the plan's provider manual, not from Subpart M (see MA-07).
rules.requires: Every provider contract must contain a prompt payment clause; the plan must pay per the contract. Contracts must hold members harmless (422.504(g)(1)(i)).
rules.deadline: Whatever the contract's prompt-payment clause says; no federal day count applies to contracted claims.
rules.consequence: Breach of contract remedies under the agreement (often arbitration). CMS can treat failure to comply with 422.520 as a contract compliance issue, but its own CTM SOP says CMS is not a party to contractual matters (MA-25).
rules.provider_use: Pull each MA contract's prompt-pay and interest clause and cite it by section in every contracted-plan letter, together with the plan's own published resolution targets (MA-30 to MA-33). Ask the plan to identify the contract term that supports any reduction.

rules.quote: 42 CFR 422.402: “The standards established under this part supersede any State law or regulation (other than State licensing laws or State laws relating to plan solvency) with respect to the MA plans that are offered by MA organizations.”
rules.applies_to: All MA plans in KY and IN, contracted or not.
rules.requires: Federal MA standards (including prompt payment and appeals) displace state law for MA plans, except state licensing and solvency laws.
rules.consequence: Kentucky and Indiana prompt-pay statutes, their interest rates and state insurance department claim-payment enforcement do not govern MA claims. Humana's 2026 manual says so too: “State laws and/or regulations do not affect the adjudication of claims for Medicare Advantage members.”
rules.provider_use: Never cite KRS/IC prompt-pay rules or threaten a state insurance department complaint on an MA claim; a payer (or its AI reviewer) will flag it and it weakens the letter. Use federal rules, the contract, and CMS channels instead. (A contract could still incorporate state law by its own terms.)

rules.citation: 42 CFR 422.568(c) and (f); 42 CFR 422.566(b)(2)-(3); Parts C&D Appeals Guidance (eff. July 6, 2026) sec. 40.10-40.11
rules.quote: 422.568(f): “If the MA organization fails to provide the enrollee and the physician or provider involved, as appropriate, with timely notice of an organization determination as specified in this section, this failure itself constitutes an adverse organization determination and may be appealed.” 422.568(c): “The MA organization must process requests for payment according to the “prompt payment” provisions set forth in § 422.520.”
rules.applies_to: All MA plans. For payment requests the deadline is the 422.520 clock, so this bites hardest for non-contracted providers (30/60 days). Guidance 40.10: for contract providers the payment timeframe is 'based on the contract terms'.
rules.requires: Issue the payment organization determination (pay or written denial) within the prompt-payment timeframe; otherwise the silence is an appealable adverse determination.
rules.deadline: Non-contracted payment request: 60 calendar days from the request (30 for clean claims to be paid).
rules.consequence: Provider (with WOL) may file a reconsideration; the plan then has 60 days to decide or must auto-forward to the IRE (MA-09).
rules.provider_use: For 'no answer' non-contracted claims past day 60, send one combined letter: (1) notice that the plan's silence is an adverse organization determination under 422.568(f); (2) a reconsideration request with signed WOL attached; (3) a reminder that the plan must decide within 60 days or forward the file to the IRE (422.590(b),(d)).

rules.citation: 42 CFR 422.574(b), 422.578, 422.582(d); Parts C&D Appeals Guidance sec. 50.1.1 and 40.12.1
rules.quote: 422.574(b): parties include “An assignee of the enrollee (that is, a physician or other provider who has furnished a service to the enrollee and formally agrees to waive any right to payment from the enrollee for that service)”. Guidance 50.1.1: “A non-contract provider, on his or her own behalf, may request a reconsideration (i.e., an appeal) for a denied claim only if the non-contract provider completes a Waiver of Liability (WOL) statement”; “a non-contracted provider does not need to receive zero payment to request a reconsideration”.
rules.applies_to: Non-contracted providers of any MA plan, post-service claims. Guidance lists full Subpart M rights for DRG/diagnosis code denials, 'Downcoding', 'Bundling issues and disputed rate of payment' and 'Level of care or rate of payment denials' (e.g., plan pays a lower visit level than billed).
rules.requires: Plan must accept a reconsideration from a non-contracted provider who signs the WOL; if the WOL is missing the plan 'should make and document reasonable efforts to obtain the missing form' before dismissing; plan 'must issue a substantive reconsideration decision within 60 days ... from when the WOL is received'. A billing agency may file without an AOR but 'may not sign the WOL on behalf of the provider'. Plan notices to non-contract providers must state the right to reconsideration, the WOL requirement (with the form or a link), and '65 calendar days from the remittance notification date'.
rules.deadline: File within 65 days of the remittance/denial notice (MA-08); plan decides within 60 days of receiving the request with WOL.
rules.consequence: Once a valid WOL is filed the enrollee has no appealable interest and all notices go to the provider; uphold or late decision goes to the IRE (MA-09).
rules.provider_use: Pre-sign a practice WOL (physician/owner signature; e-signature allowed via a compliant plan portal) and attach it to every non-contracted MA appeal, including partial payments, E/M downcodes and bundling edits. Where a plan manual says non-par providers may appeal only full or zero-pay denials (Humana 2026 manual) or only denials 'with member liability' (Anthem 2027 guidebook), quote guidance 50.1.1 back to them.

rules.citation: 42 CFR 422.562(c)(2) (revised by 90 FR 15910, Apr. 15, 2025; revised text appears in eCFR from June 3, 2025); Parts C&D Appeals Guidance sec. 50.1 note
rules.quote: 422.562(c)(2): “If a contract provider's request for payment has been adjudicated and the enrollee is determined to have no further liability to pay for the services furnished by the MA organization, the claim payment determination is not subject to the appeal process in this subpart.” Guidance: “Contract provider disputes involving plan payment denials are governed by the appeals/dispute resolution provisions in the contract between the provider and the plan.”
rules.applies_to: Contracted providers' post-service payment denials and reductions in MA plans where the member owes nothing further. Before June 3, 2025 the paragraph read: 'If an enrollee has no further liability to pay for services that were furnished by an MA organization, a determination regarding these services is not subject to appeal.' The revision limited the bar to contract providers, which confirms non-contracted providers keep appeal rights.
rules.requires: No Subpart M reconsideration, no IRE, no ALJ for these; disputes go through the contract and plan manual process.
rules.deadline: Per contract/plan manual (see MA-30 to MA-33).
rules.consequence: The IRE, Star Ratings appeal measures (C30/C31) and ALJ path are not available for contracted payment disputes. A contracted physician can still request PRE-service organization determinations and reconsiderations for the patient (422.566(c), 422.578), which do go to the IRE if upheld.
rules.provider_use: RemitWatch must tag each MA claim as contracted or non-contracted for that specific plan/product before choosing a letter. For contracted plans, do not claim IRE rights; use the contract, the plan's own timelines, the CMS UM rules (MA-18 to MA-21) and the CTM complaint form (MA-25). Push pre-service disputes (prior authorization) through the physician's right to request reconsideration, which does carry IRE/Star Ratings weight.

rules.citation: 42 CFR 422.582(a)-(c); Parts C&D Appeals Guidance sec. 50.3
rules.quote: 422.582(b): “a request for reconsideration must be filed within 60 calendar days after receipt of the written organization determination notice. (1) The date of receipt of the organization determination is presumed to be 5 calendar days after the date of the written organization determination, unless there is evidence to the contrary.”
rules.applies_to: Parties to an MA organization determination: enrollee, non-contracted provider with WOL, treating physician for pre-service requests.
rules.requires: Written request (plan may accept oral). Late filing allowed for good cause if the request is in writing and states why it was late (422.582(c)); guidance 50.3 examples include not receiving the notice or receiving it late, incorrect or incomplete information about the appeal process, and documentation difficult to locate.
rules.deadline: 60 days after receipt of the notice; receipt presumed 5 days after the notice date, so effectively 65 calendar days from the notice/remittance date. Filed on the date the plan receives it.
rules.consequence: Untimely requests without good cause are dismissed (422.582(f)(3)); dismissal is reviewable by the IRE (MA-12).
rules.provider_use: Docket 65 days from each remittance date. For late items, add a good-cause paragraph (e.g., plan's remittance lacked the required appeal-rights/WOL language from guidance 40.12.1, or notice not received). UHC's non-contracted sheet says 60 days from the denial date; cite 422.582(b)(1) if UHC dismisses a filing made on days 61-65.

rules.quote: 422.590(b)(2): “If the MA organization affirms, in whole or in part, its adverse organization determination, it must prepare a written explanation and send the case file to the independent entity contracted by CMS no later than 60 calendar days from the date it receives the request for a standard reconsideration.” 422.590(d): failure to meet the timeframe “constitutes an affirmation of its adverse organization determination, and the MA organization must submit the file to the independent entity”.
rules.applies_to: MA plans deciding payment reconsiderations from enrollees or non-contracted providers with WOL (not contracted-provider payment disputes, MA-07).
rules.requires: Decide a payment reconsideration and, if fully favorable, issue it and pay within 60 calendar days of receiving the request (422.590(b)(1), 422.618(a)(2)); if upheld in any part or not decided in time, send a written explanation and the complete case file to the CMS Part C IRE within 60 calendar days. Plans 'are not required to notify beneficiaries upon forwarding cases' (guidance 50.7.2).
rules.deadline: 60 calendar days from plan receipt of the reconsideration (from WOL receipt if the WOL came later, guidance 50.1.1). If the IRE reverses, plan must pay within 30 calendar days of the IRE notice (422.618(b)(2)).
rules.consequence: Auto-forward to the IRE (MA-13). Late forwards count against Star Ratings measure C30 and IRE overturns against C31 (MA-26). Guidance 50.7.2: a 'pattern of not processing level 1 appeals within the required timeframes' may be 'out of compliance with the terms of its Medicare contract and/or subject to intermediate sanctions'.
rules.provider_use: Each reconsideration letter should state the 60-day decision clock and the plan's duty to forward the file to the IRE if it upholds or misses the clock; at day 61 send a short notice that the file is now due at the IRE and check the C2C appeal-status site. Track IRE outcomes per plan; overturn rates are evidence for CMS complaints.

rules.citation: 42 CFR 422.590(h)(2); 42 U.S.C. 1395w-22(g)(2)(B); Parts C&D Appeals Guidance sec. 50.6
rules.quote: 422.590(h)(2): “When the issue is the MA organization's denial of coverage based on a lack of medical necessity (or any substantively equivalent term used to describe the concept of medical necessity), the reconsidered determination must be made by a physician with expertise in the field of medicine that is appropriate for the services at issue.” Statute: “shall be made only by a physician with appropriate expertise in the field of medicine which necessitates treatment who is other than a physician involved in the initial determination.”
rules.applies_to: All MA reconsiderations of medical-necessity denials (enrollee, non-contracted provider, treating physician pre-service). Not contracted-provider payment disputes outside Subpart M, although the plan's own UM duties still apply (MA-11).
rules.requires: A physician (not just a nurse, coder or software) with expertise appropriate to the service, not involved in the first decision, must make the reconsideration; need not be the same specialty but must have 'the appropriate level of training and expertise' (guidance 50.6).
rules.deadline: Within the reconsideration clock (MA-09).
rules.consequence: A reconsideration not made by a qualified physician is noncompliant and is a CMS program audit target (ODAG reviews per CMS FAQ of Feb. 6, 2024, Q14).
rules.provider_use: For Mohs, radiation and pathology medical-necessity denials, ask that the reconsideration be decided by a physician with dermatologic surgery / radiation oncology / dermatopathology expertise as appropriate, cite 422.590(h)(2), and ask the plan to identify the reviewer's specialty in its decision.

rules.citation: 42 CFR 422.566(b)(3), (d); 42 CFR 422.562(a)(4); CMS HPMS memo FAQ on CMS-4201-F (Feb. 6, 2024) Q9
rules.quote: 422.566(d): “If the MA organization expects to issue a partially or fully adverse medical necessity ... decision based on the initial review of the request, the organization determination must be reviewed by a physician or other appropriate health care professional with expertise in the field of medicine or health care that is appropriate for the services at issue, including knowledge of Medicare coverage criteria, before the MA organization issues the organization determination decision.” FAQ Q9: “the refusal to provide or pay for services, in whole or in part, including the type or level of services ... is an organization determination by the MA plan under § 422.566(b)(3).”
rules.applies_to: All MA plans, every initial medical-necessity denial or reduction (pre-service, concurrent or post-service, including post-payment 'payment reviews'), whether the provider is contracted or not.
rules.requires: Physician/appropriate professional review with relevant expertise before any adverse medical-necessity decision; medical director responsible for clinical accuracy (422.562(a)(4)). Post-claim audits must follow reopening rules (FAQ Q9).
rules.deadline: Before the denial issues.
rules.consequence: Noncompliant determinations are CMS audit findings (ODAG); for parties with appeal rights, a reconsideration must follow.
rules.provider_use: When a remittance reduces a level of service or denies for 'not medically necessary' with no sign of clinician review, ask the plan to confirm in writing which physician or professional reviewed it and their field, citing 422.566(d) and the CMS FAQ; for contracted plans this goes in the contract dispute and, if refused, in a CTM complaint.

rules.citation: 42 CFR 422.582(f)-(i); 42 CFR 422.590(i); 42 CFR 422.592(i); Parts C&D Appeals Guidance sec. 50.9; CMS Part C IRE page
rules.quote: Guidance 50.9: “The above list of circumstances (taken from the applicable regulations) under which a plan must dismiss a request for a level 1 appeal is exhaustive. A plan may not deem a request invalid or dismiss a request for a level 1 appeal for any reason not explicitly included in 42 CFR §§ 422.582(f) and 423.582(e), as applicable.”
rules.applies_to: MA reconsideration requests by enrollees, representatives and non-contracted providers.
rules.requires: Plan may dismiss only for the listed reasons (not a proper party, invalid request, untimely without good cause, death with no financial interest, withdrawal); before dismissing a non-contracted request for a missing WOL it should try to obtain it. Dismissal notice must state the reason, the right to ask the plan to vacate, and the right to IRE review (422.582(g)).
rules.deadline: IRE review of a dismissal: 422.590(i) says within 60 calendar days of the dismissal notice; CMS's IRE page says 'within 65 calendar days from the date of the plan dismissal decision notice'. Plan may vacate within 6 months for good cause (422.582(h)).
rules.consequence: If the IRE finds the dismissal wrong it vacates and remands for a plan reconsideration (422.592(i)).
rules.provider_use: Challenge any dismissal for reasons outside 422.582(f) (wrong form, no AOR from a WOL provider, 'use the dispute process instead') by asking the plan to vacate and filing IRE dismissal review (C2C, fax (904) 539-4080, phone 1-866-320-0963) within 60 days of the dismissal notice.

rules.citation: 42 CFR 422.592, 422.594, 422.596, 422.618(b)(2); 42 U.S.C. 1395w-22(g)(4); CMS 'Reconsideration by Part C Independent Review Entity (IRE)' page (modified 05/01/2026)
rules.quote: CMS IRE page: “Effective May 1, 2026, C2C Innovative Solutions, Inc. (C2C) is the Part C IRE.” “Once the case file or appeal is received by the IRE, the IRE must make its decision ... no later than the following timeframes: ... Payments requests: 60 calendar days”.
rules.applies_to: Cases the MA plan upholds (in whole or part) or fails to decide on time, from enrollees or non-contracted providers with WOL.
rules.requires: IRE decides payment reconsiderations within 60 calendar days (extension of up to 14 days only in listed cases); IRE notice must give reasons and ALJ rights (422.594). If the IRE reverses, the plan must pay within 30 calendar days of the notice and tell the IRE it has done so (422.618(b)(2)).
rules.deadline: IRE: 60 calendar days from its receipt of the case file (payment). Plan effectuation of IRE reversal: 30 calendar days.
rules.consequence: IRE decision binds the plan (422.596); the plan cannot appeal to an ALJ (422.600(a) excludes the MA organization). Each case also feeds Star Ratings C30/C31 (MA-26).
rules.provider_use: Track IRE status via C2C's Part C appeal-status lookup (https://partcappeals.c2cinc.com/Search-Appeal-Status per the 2027 Star Technical Notes); docket 30 days after any IRE reversal to confirm payment, then send a non-effectuation letter citing 422.618(b)(2) and copy the IRE.

rules.quote: CMS ALJ page: “For calendar year 2026, the amount in controversy threshold is $200. For calendar year 2027, the amount in controversy will remain $200.” Fed. Reg. 2026-19016: the judicial review amount “will increase from $1,960 for CY 2026 to $2,000 for CY 2027.” Guidance 70.2: “For Parts C and D, appeals may be aggregated to meet the AIC. See §§ 405.1006(e) and (f)”.
rules.applies_to: Parties to an IRE reconsideration other than the MA organization (enrollee, non-contracted provider with WOL).
rules.requires: ALJ hearing if amount remaining in controversy meets the threshold; request in writing (form OMHA-100) within 60 days of receipt of the IRE notice (receipt presumed 5 days after its date). A single appellant may aggregate claims involving 'similar or related services' if the aggregation request is filed within 60 days after receipt of all the reconsiderations (405.1006(e)(1)). If an ALJ or higher reverses, plan must pay within 60 calendar days unless it seeks Council review (422.618(c)).
rules.deadline: 60 days from receipt of the IRE decision; effectuation 60 days after an ALJ reversal.
rules.consequence: ALJ/Council decisions bind the plan; the plan may seek Council review.
rules.provider_use: Small upheld IRE claims of the same kind (e.g., a plan's systematic E/M or Mohs-add-on reduction) can be bundled into one ALJ request once they total $200, which makes even sub-dollar lines worth carrying when they ride along in a batch.

rules.citation: 42 CFR 422.616; 42 CFR 405.980(a)(3), (c); 42 CFR 405.986; Parts C&D Appeals Guidance sec. 80.1-80.3.2
rules.quote: 422.616(b): “Reopening may be at the instigation of any party.” 405.980(c): a party may request reopening “(1) ... within 1 year from the date of the initial determination ... for any reason. (2) ... within 4 years ... for good cause ... (3) ... at any time if the initial determination is unfavorable, in whole or in part, to the party thereto, but only for the purpose of correcting a clerical error”. Guidance 80.3.2: “the reopening action should be completed within 60 days from the date of receipt of the party's reopening request.”
rules.applies_to: MA organization determinations and reconsiderations; parties (enrollee, non-contracted provider with WOL). For contracted providers, reopening is a plan practice (e.g., Humana's dispute/reopening wording) rather than a Subpart M right because 422.562(c)(2) removes their payment disputes from Subpart M.
rules.requires: Plan may reopen on request within the 405.980 windows; clerical errors (math, data entry, duplicate denials) are handled as reopenings (405.980(a)(3)). No reopening while an appeal is pending; plan cannot reopen after forwarding the case to the IRE (guidance 80.2). Decision whether to reopen is not appealable, but a revised adverse decision is.
rules.deadline: Request: 1 year (any reason), 4 years (good cause), any time (clerical error on an unfavorable determination). Plan completion target: 60 days.
rules.consequence: Revised determinations restart appeal rights for the revised part only.
rules.provider_use: Cheapest route for small clerical items past the 65-day appeal window (wrong units, wrong modifier processing, duplicate denials): send batch reopening requests for clerical error, citing 405.980(c)(3) and 422.616.

rules.citation: 42 CFR 422.568(d)-(e); 42 U.S.C. 1395w-22(g)(1)(B); Parts C&D Appeals Guidance sec. 40.12.1
rules.quote: 422.568(e): “The notice of any denial under paragraph (d) of this section must— (1) Use approved notice language in a readable and understandable form; (2) State the specific reasons for the denial; (3) Inform the enrollee of his or her right to a reconsideration”. Guidance 40.12.1 (IDN): “A specific and detailed explanation of why the medical services, items or Part B drugs were denied, including a description of the applicable coverage rule or applicable plan policy”. Non-contract providers: plan “must notify the non-contract provider of the specific reason for the denial and provide a description of the appeals process.”
rules.applies_to: All MA plans. Enrollee denials use the IDN (CMS-10003-NDMCP) or an EOB with the verbatim IDN language; non-contracted provider denials use a remittance or similar notice with the elements in guidance 40.12.1 (the IDN itself may not be used for them). Contracted providers: remittance terms come from the contract.
rules.requires: Written notice to the enrollee and the physician/provider 'as appropriate' for any full or partial denial; specific reasons; appeal rights. Non-contract provider remittance must state: right to reconsideration; WOL requirement with the form or a direct link; '65 calendar days from the remittance notification date'; what to include; where to send. ABN (CMS-R-131) may not be used in MA.
rules.deadline: Within the organization-determination timeframe.
rules.consequence: Defective or missing notice: supports good cause for late appeals (guidance 50.3 lists not receiving the notice and incorrect information about the process); no timely notice = adverse determination (MA-05); CTM complaint material.
rules.provider_use: Flag remittances that deny with only a CARC/RARC and no appeal-rights/WOL language. In the appeal, demand the specific coverage rule relied on and note that the notice lacked required elements, which also preserves good cause for any late filing.

rules.quote: 422.122(a): “Beginning January 1, 2026, if the MA organization denies a prior authorization request ... the response to the provider must include a specific reason for the denial, regardless of the method used to communicate that information.” 422.568(b)(1)(ii): “Beginning on or after January 1, 2026, for a service or item subject to the prior authorization rules in § 422.122, 7 calendar days after receiving the request”.
rules.applies_to: All MA coordinated care plans; any provider (contracted or not) requesting a pre-service decision; physicians may request expedited decisions regardless of affiliation.
rules.requires: Standard PA decisions within 7 calendar days (14 days for items not under 422.122), expedited within 72 hours; plan must expedite when a physician indicates the standard time could seriously jeopardize life, health or ability to regain maximum function; specific denial reason to the provider; no punitive action against a physician who requests or supports an expedited decision or reconsideration (422.570(f), 422.584(f)).
rules.deadline: 7 calendar days (standard, PA items, from Jan 1, 2026), 14 days (other items), 72 hours (expedited); extensions of up to 14 days only in listed cases.
rules.consequence: Missed deadline = adverse organization determination appealable to the plan and then the IRE (422.568(f), 422.572(f)); pre-service reconsiderations requested by the treating physician go to the IRE if upheld, even for contracted physicians.
rules.provider_use: For Mohs, radiation courses and other PA items, log request time; at day 8 (or 73 hours) treat silence as a denial and file a physician reconsideration; demand the specific denial reason required by 422.122(a).

rules.citation: 42 CFR 422.101(b)(6) and (c)(1)(i) (CY2024 final rule CMS-4201-F; eCFR source note 88 FR 22328, Apr. 12, 2023); CMS HPMS memo FAQ on CMS-4201-F (Feb. 6, 2024) Q2
rules.quote: 422.101(c)(1)(i): medical necessity determinations must be based on “(A) Coverage and benefit criteria as specified at paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section and may not deny coverage for basic benefits based on coverage criteria not specified in paragraph (b) or (c)”; “(C) The enrollee's medical history (for example, diagnoses, conditions, functional status), physician recommendations, and clinical notes.” FAQ Q2: “an algorithm that determines coverage based on a larger data set instead of the individual patient's medical history, the physician's recommendations, or clinical notes would not be compliant with § 422.101(c).” “Because publicly posted coverage criteria are static and unchanging, artificial intelligence cannot be used to shift the coverage criteria over time.”
rules.applies_to: All MA plans' medical-necessity decisions on Part A/B basic benefits (Mohs, radiation, pathology, E/M), contracted and non-contracted providers alike.
rules.requires: Follow NCDs, LCDs of the local MAC (CGS J15 for KY, WPS J8 for IN under 422.101(b)(3)) and Original Medicare rules; internal criteria only when Medicare criteria are 'not fully established', and then publicly accessible with an evidence summary, sources and rationale (422.101(b)(6)(ii)); decide on the individual patient's record, not a population model.
rules.consequence: Noncompliant denials are CMS program audit targets (FAQ Q14: physician reviewers check denied requests against NCDs/LCDs and posted internal criteria). For parties with appeal rights, grounds for reversal at the plan or IRE.
rules.provider_use: In every medical-necessity or level-of-care dispute ask the plan to name (1) the NCD/LCD/statute or (2) the publicly posted internal criterion with its evidence summary that the denial relied on, and state that a decision made by an algorithm or on criteria not specified in 422.101(b)-(c) without review of this patient's notes violates 422.101(c)(1)(i). Attach the note and map it to the LCD criteria.

rules.citation: 42 CFR 422.138(b)-(c) (as amended 90 FR 15910, Apr. 15, 2025); CMS HPMS memo FAQ (Feb. 6, 2024) Q9; Parts C&D Appeals Guidance sec. 80.3.1 note
rules.quote: 422.138(c): “If the MA organization approved the furnishing of a covered item or service through a prior authorization or pre-service determination of coverage or payment, or a concurrent determination made during the enrollee's receipt of inpatient or outpatient services, it may not deny coverage later on the basis of lack of medical necessity and may not reopen such a decision for any reason except for good cause ... or if there is reliable evidence of fraud or similar fault”.
rules.applies_to: All MA coordinated care plans; contracted and non-contracted providers.
rules.requires: An approved PA/pre-service/concurrent decision cannot later be denied for lack of medical necessity; reopening only for good cause (new and material evidence or obvious error, 405.986) or fraud/similar fault. PA may be used only to confirm diagnoses/criteria or medical necessity under 422.101(c)(1) (422.138(b)).
rules.consequence: Post-payment medical-necessity takebacks of authorized services violate 422.138(c); CMS audit target.
rules.provider_use: Match every MA medical-necessity denial or recoupment against the authorization log; if an approval exists, the letter cites 422.138(c) and the authorization number and demands reversal; for contracted plans this goes in the dispute and a CTM complaint if refused.

rules.quote: 422.112(b)(8)(i): “(A) Approval of a prior authorization request for a course of treatment must be valid for as long as medically necessary to avoid disruptions in care, in accordance with applicable coverage criteria, the individual patient's medical history, and the treating provider's recommendation; and (B) A minimum 90-day transition period for any active course(s) of treatment when an enrollee has enrolled in an MA plan after starting a course of treatment, even if the service is furnished by an out-of-network provider.”
rules.applies_to: MA coordinated care plans; basic benefits; enrollees in an active course of treatment (e.g., a radiation therapy course for skin cancer). The 90-day transition applies even to out-of-network providers.
rules.requires: PA for a course of treatment must cover the whole medically necessary course; new plan enrollees mid-course get at least 90 days without reauthorization or disruption.
rules.deadline: Minimum 90 days from enrollment for new enrollees mid-course.
rules.consequence: Denials of later fractions/visits for lack of reauthorization during the course or transition period are contrary to the rule; appealable by parties; CMS audit/complaint material.
rules.provider_use: For radiation courses spanning a plan change (January 1 enrollment switches), cite 422.112(b)(8)(i)(B) when a new MA plan denies continuing fractions for lack of PA within 90 days of enrollment.

rules.quote: 422.137(b): “An MA plan may not use any UM policies and procedures for basic or supplemental benefits on or after January 1, 2024 unless those policies and procedures have been reviewed and approved by the UM committee.” 422.202(b)(1): practice and UM guidelines “(i) Are based on current evidence in widely used treatment guidelines or clinical literature; ... (iii) Are developed in consultation with contracting physicians”; (3) “Decisions with respect to utilization management ... are consistent with the guidelines.”
rules.applies_to: MA plans using UM (prior authorization, claim edits used as UM). 422.202(b) consultation duties run to contracting physicians.
rules.requires: UM policies approved annually by a physician-majority UM committee that checks them against 422.101(b), 422.138, 422.202(b)(1) and 422.101(c)(1) and documents its reasons (available to CMS); guidelines communicated to providers; UM decisions consistent with them; written policies 'that allow for individual medical necessity determinations' (422.112(a)(6)(ii)).
rules.deadline: Annual UM committee review.
rules.consequence: A UM policy not approved by the committee may not be used; CMS audit target (FAQ Q14).
rules.provider_use: Contracted practice can ask, as a contracting physician, for the guideline and the UM committee approval behind a recurring denial/edit (e.g., a Mohs or E/M edit) and for consultation under 422.202(b); refusal supports a CTM complaint and RO contact.

rules.citation: 42 CFR 422.100(b)(2); 42 CFR 422.214(a)(1); CMS 'Provider Payment Dispute Resolution for Non-Contracted Providers' page; CMS MA Payment Guide for Out of Network Payments (4/15/2015) 'Physician Services'
rules.quote: CMS page: “Medicare Advantage organizations, Cost plans, and PACE organizations are required to reimburse non-contract providers for Part A and Part B services provided to Medicare beneficiaries with an amount that is no less than the amount that would be paid under original Medicare.” Guide: physicians “are paid using the lesser of billed charges, or the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS)”; non-participating fee schedule “is 95% of the participating physician fee schedule.”
rules.applies_to: Non-contracted providers of MA plans for covered services the plan must pay (PPO out-of-network benefits, emergency/urgent, plan-authorized or plan-arranged care, and services found covered on appeal, 422.100(b)(1)(v)). Not contracted providers (contract rate applies).
rules.requires: Plan pays at least the Original Medicare amount (MPFS for the locality, modifiers and MPPR rules as in Original Medicare); provider must accept that as payment in full (422.214(a)(1)).
rules.deadline: Payment timing per MA-01.
rules.consequence: Underpayment below the Original Medicare amount is disputable with the plan and, as a partial payment/level-of-care issue, appealable with WOL (guidance 50.1.1) to the IRE.
rules.provider_use: RemitWatch can price every non-contracted MA line against the CGS J15 (KY) / WPS J8 (IN) MPFS locality amount and generate a bulk underpayment list per plan; send as a plan dispute and, for items not fixed, as WOL reconsiderations.

rules.citation: CMS MA Payment Guide for Out of Network Payments (4/15/2015 update) p.35; CMS 'Provider Payment Dispute Resolution for Non-Contracted Providers' page (modified 09/10/2024)
rules.quote: Guide: “From 2009 until January 31, 2014, CMS contracted the services of C2C Solutions, Inc., an independent entity, to adjudicate payment disputes between non-contracted providers, MAOs and other payers. As of January 31, 2014, providers should contact the MAO or other payer directly to dispute payments.” “If a provider has exhausted the plan's internal dispute process and still maintains it has not been reimbursed fairly, it may file a complaint through 1-800-Medicare”. CMS page: “CMS Account Managers have been instructed to closely monitor MAOs' actions in this regard and will take compliance actions as necessary.”
rules.applies_to: Non-contracted providers disputing MA payment amounts.
rules.requires: No independent CMS payment-dispute contractor exists now; dispute with the plan first; then CMS complaint routes (1-800-MEDICARE, provider complaint form, Regional Office). No current Medicare Managed Care Manual chapter on a PDR process was found (Chapter 13 now only points to the appeals guidance webpage).
rules.deadline: Plan-set dispute windows (e.g., UHC 120 days from initial payment, UHC responds in 30 days).
rules.consequence: CMS compliance action through account managers (no stated timeline).
rules.provider_use: Do not cite the old PDRC process or its 2010 manual. For amount disputes use the plan's dispute process and, where the reduction is a partial payment/level-of-care/bundling issue, the WOL reconsideration path (which reaches the IRE). Escalate unresolved patterns via the CMS provider complaint form and the Regional Office, citing the CMS page's statement about account managers.

rules.quote: 422.125(b): “(1) ... The MA organization must resolve immediate need complaints within 2 calendar days of the assignment date. (2) ... urgent complaints within 7 calendar days of the assignment date. (3) ... all other complaints within 30 calendar days of the assignment date.” (c): “the MA organization must attempt to contact the individual who filed a complaint within 7 calendar days of the assignment date.”
rules.applies_to: All MA organizations, for complaints CMS records in the Complaints Tracking Module and assigns to the plan, including complaints from providers.
rules.requires: Resolve CTM complaints within 2/7/30 calendar days of assignment and try to contact the complainant within 7 days; 422.504(a)(15) makes this a contract term.
rules.deadline: 30 calendar days from CMS assignment (claims-payment complaints are normally 'all other'); contact within 7 days.
rules.consequence: Failure is a breach of the CMS contract (422.504(a)(15)); complaint volume feeds Star Ratings C27 (MA-26).
rules.provider_use: After the plan's own process fails, file through the CMS provider complaint form (MA-25); the plan then owes a contact within 7 days and a resolution within 30 days of assignment. Letters can say truthfully that unresolved items will be reported to CMS through the Complaints Tracking Module.

rules.citation: CMS HPMS memo 'HPMS Complaints Tracking Module Updates for Managing Provider Complaints' (Dec. 22, 2025); CMS 'Provider Complaints Form' page; CMS HPMS memo 'Updated Complaints Tracking Module Standard Operating Procedures' (Jan. 6, 2025) App. A; Parts C&D Appeals Guidance sec. 30
rules.url: https://www.cms.gov/medicare/health-drug-plans/provider-complaints-form | https://leadingage.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/CTM_Provider_Complaint_HPMS_Memo.pdf (copy of CMS memo) | https://ncpa.org/sites/default/files/2025-01/CTMSOP01062025.pdf (copy of CMS SOP) | https://www.cms.gov/medicare/appeals-and-grievances/mmcag/downloads/parts-c-and-d-enrollee-grievances-organization-coverage-determinations-and-appeals-guidance.pdf
rules.quote: Dec. 22, 2025 memo: “CMS will implement an online form on cms.gov for providers that need to report a complaint about a Medicare Advantage plan. Upon submission, these complaints will be sent to the HPMS Complaints Tracking Module (CTM).” SOP: “CMS is not a party to contractual matters and expects plans to resolve these complaints with the providers directly.” App. A lists “Provider Specific • 2.70: Improper, insufficient, or delayed claims payment” without the “(EX)” exclusion mark. Guidance sec. 30: providers “may contact their local CMS Regional Office or submit an online complaint on cms.gov.”
rules.applies_to: Any provider (contracted or not) with a complaint about an MA plan, after using the plan's dispute process.
rules.requires: Online form (cms.gov > Medicare > Health & drug plans > Report a provider complaint about an MA plan) captures complainant, beneficiary, provider, plan, summary, optional dates of service and claim number; CMS reviews/triages, then assigns to the contract; plan must resolve per 422.125 and document efforts to resolve with the provider. The form warns not to use special characters such as quotes.
rules.deadline: Plan resolution 30 days from CMS assignment (422.125).
rules.consequence: Assigned plan-lead complaints count in Star Ratings C27 unless in an excluded subcategory (inference from the SOP exclusion rule; not confirmed for provider-form complaints).
rules.provider_use: Use for patterns (many claims, same plan, same reason), not single small claims; summarize counts, dollars, dates and the rule broken. The prior letter can state that if the plan does not resolve by a date the practice will file through the CMS provider complaint form. Expect CMS to decline pure contract-rate disputes.

rules.citation: CMS 2027 Medicare Part C & D Star Ratings Technical Notes (last updated 11/04/2026), measures C27, C30, C31 and Table G-1
rules.quote: C30/C31: “This measure includes all Standard Coverage, Standard Claim, and Expedited appeals received by the IRE, regardless of the appellant. This includes appeals requested by a beneficiary, appeals requested by a party on behalf of a beneficiary, and appeals requested by non-contract providers.” C27 metric: “Total number of all complaints logged into the Complaints Tracking Module (CTM)” per 1,000 members.
rules.applies_to: MA contracts (Humana, Anthem, UHC, Wellcare MA contracts). Appeals measures reflect only cases that reach the IRE (so not contracted-provider payment disputes, MA-07).
rules.requires: C30 'Plan Makes Timely Decisions about Appeals' = share of IRE cases the plan forwarded on time (5 stars only at 100%; 4 stars 98% to <100%; 1 star below 79%); C31 'Reviewing Appeals Decisions' = share of IRE-reviewed cases upheld; C27 = CTM complaint rate. Each has weight 2.
rules.deadline: Measured by calendar year of IRE receipt (2027 Star Ratings use 2025 data).
rules.consequence: Late forwards, IRE overturns and complaints reduce Star Ratings, which drive MA quality bonus payments and rebates (bonus mechanics not researched here).
rules.provider_use: State truthfully in non-contracted appeal letters that if the plan upholds, the file goes to the CMS IRE and that the plan's on-time forwarding and IRE outcomes are CMS Star Ratings measures. Track each plan's late forwards and overturns to support CMS complaints.

rules.quote: 422.510(a)(4): CMS may terminate if the MA organization “(ii) Substantially failed to comply with the requirements in subpart M of this part relating to grievances and appeals. ... (v) Substantially failed to comply with the prompt payment requirements in § 422.520.” 422.760(b)(1): “up to $25,000 as adjusted annually under 45 CFR part 102 for each determination.”
rules.applies_to: MA organizations; enforced only by CMS/OIG.
rules.requires: Compliance with Subpart M and 422.520; CMS may impose intermediate sanctions (suspension of enrollment, of payment for new enrollees, or of communication activities, 422.750(a)) and CMPs for 422.510(a) determinations (422.752(b)-(c)); per-enrollee CMPs and up to $10,000/week (adjusted) for uncorrected deficiencies (422.760(b)(2),(4)); direct payment of providers and offset (1395w-27(f)(2)).
rules.consequence: Contract termination, sanctions, CMPs, direct payment with offset.
rules.provider_use: These are CMS's remedies, not the practice's. Letters can say accurately that substantial failure to meet 422.520 or Subpart M is a ground for CMS sanctions and that the practice reports unresolved patterns to CMS; do not threaten penalties the practice cannot impose.

rules.citation: CMS Regional Offices page (modified 02/26/2026); Parts C&D Appeals Guidance sec. 30
rules.quote: “Region 4 Atlanta ROATLORA@cms.hhs.gov Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, ...” “Region 5 Chicago ROCHIORA@cms.hhs.gov Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Minnesota, Ohio, Wisconsin”.
rules.applies_to: Providers in KY (Region 4) and IN (Region 5) with unresolved MA plan problems.
rules.requires: Centralized mail: CMS, Office of Program Operations and Local Engagement, 7500 Security Boulevard, Mail Stop DO-01-40, Baltimore, MD 21244-1850.
rules.deadline: None stated.
rules.consequence: Regional staff can route issues; no stated authority or timeline for individual claim resolution.
rules.provider_use: Copy the RO mailbox on pattern escalations (never PHI in plain email; summarize de-identified counts) after the plan's process and the CTM form.

rules.quote: 422.633(f)(1): “The applicable integrated plan must resolve integrated reconsiderations as expeditiously as the enrollee's health condition requires but no later than 30 calendar days from the date of receipt of the request for the integrated reconsideration.”
rules.applies_to: Only 'applicable integrated plans' (certain FIDE/HIDE D-SNPs with exclusively aligned Medicaid enrollment). Not confirmed which, if any, KY/IN D-SNPs (Humana, Anthem, UHC, Wellcare) qualify.
rules.requires: Integrated process replaces 422.566(c)-(d), 422.568-422.590 and 422.618(a): file within 60 days of receipt (receipt presumed 5 days after notice); one level of plan reconsideration resolved within 30 calendar days (extendable 14 days); assignee provider with WOL is a party (422.629(l)(4)(i)).
rules.deadline: 30 calendar days for the plan's integrated reconsideration.
rules.consequence: Unfavorable integrated reconsiderations go to the next Medicare/Medicaid level as described in the notice.
rules.provider_use: Before applying the 60-day MA clock to a dual-eligible MA member, check whether the plan is an applicable integrated plan; if so the plan's clock is 30 days.

rules.citation: Humana 2026 Provider Manual for physicians, hospitals and healthcare providers (non-delegated), 'Provider Claims Dispute Process' and 'Member Grievance/Appeal Process'; Humana 'Grievances and Appeals/Inquiry Directory' (954306ALL0226)
rules.quote: “Claims disputes must be received by Humana within 18 months from the date the provider received notice of the original claim determination unless state or federal law or the agreement requires another time period”. “A nonparticipating provider can appeal claim denials for Medicare members only with a waiver of liability form for the following: • Full claim denials • Claims paying zero dollars • Claims denied for medical necessity • Claims denied for noncovered benefits”. Directory: “Please submit your appeal request in writing within 65 calendar days from the date of the denial notice.”
rules.applies_to: Humana MA. Contracted providers: dispute process (Availity 'Dispute Claim', 800-448-6262, Humana Correspondence P.O. Box 14601 Lexington KY 40512), escalation to HumanaProviderServices@humana.com. Non-par: Humana Grievance and Appeal Department, P.O. Box 14165, Lexington, KY 40512-4165, with WOL.
rules.requires: Dispute must include the proposed correct payment amount and the difference; 'Multiple provider dispute requests per provider encounter are generally unacceptable' without new material information. Inquiries: 'Most inquiries receive a response in 30 to 45 days'.
rules.deadline: Contracted dispute: 18 months from notice of the original determination. Non-par appeal: 65 calendar days from the denial notice.
rules.consequence: Humana's narrower non-par appeal list conflicts with CMS guidance 50.1.1 (partial payments, downcoding, bundling also appealable).
rules.provider_use: For Humana contracted claims, the 18-month window makes old underpayments still disputable; put the expected-vs-paid math in every dispute. For non-par Humana claims, cite guidance 50.1.1 when Humana refuses to treat a partial payment/downcode as appealable.

rules.citation: UnitedHealthcare 2026 Care Provider Administrative Guide ch.10 'Claim reconsideration and appeals process' and 'Resolving potential reimbursement issues'; UHC 'Non-contracted care provider dispute and appeal rights' (PCA-1-24-03448-POE-QRG_01092025)
rules.quote: Admin Guide: “You must submit your reconsideration and appeal to us within 12 months from the date of the original claim EOB or PRA (or as required by law or your Agreement).” “a Notice of Dispute must be sent no later than 60 days after the date of our decision on your appeal.” Non-contracted sheet: “You must file a dispute within 120 calendar days from the initial payment.” “UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage has 30 calendar days to review and respond after receiving a payment dispute request.” “UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage has 60 calendar days to review and respond after receiving a completed payment reconsideration (appeal) request.”
rules.applies_to: UHC MA (and commercial for the Admin Guide). Contracted: 2-step reconsideration then appeal within a combined 12 months; bulk 'Claims Research Project' for 20+ claims with the same administrative issue; Notice of Dispute (arbitration path) within 60 days of the appeal decision or the right is waived. Non-contracted: payment dispute 120 days via portal; payment reconsideration with WOL ('60 days from the denial date').
rules.requires: Non-contracted reconsiderations upheld in any part must be forwarded to the CMS IRE (UHC's own sheet).
rules.deadline: Contracted: 12 months; Notice of Dispute 60 days after appeal decision. Non-contracted: dispute 120 days; UHC answers in 30; reconsideration decided in 60.
rules.consequence: Missing the Notice of Dispute deadline 'will result in the waiver of your right to initiate dispute resolution and waiver of your right to pursue such claim or issue in any forum.'
rules.provider_use: Use UHC's Claims Research Project to submit 20+ same-issue contracted reconsiderations at once (fits the sub-dollar batch strategy). Docket the 60-day Notice of Dispute after each UHC appeal denial worth pursuing. For non-contracted UHC claims, file reconsiderations within 60 days to avoid a fight, but cite 422.582(b)(1) for days 61-65.

rules.citation: Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield Medicare Advantage Provider Guidebook, effective January 1, 2027 (Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield-CR-PM-017345-26-GRP4605), sections 5.1-5.5, 6, 7
rules.url: https://www.anthem.com/content/dam/digital/docs/provider/commercial/manuals/ABSCRPM-0010-20.pdf (linked as 'Medicare Advantage Provider Manual, Effective January 1, 2027' from https://www.anthem.com/ky/provider/individual-commercial/policies/manuals)
rules.quote: 5.3: “We accept reconsideration requests in writing, verbally and through our provider website within 120 calendar days from the date on the Explanation of Payment (EOP)”; “The plan will make every effort to resolve the claims payment reconsideration within 45 calendar days of receipt.” 5.4: appeals “within 30 calendar days of the date on the reconsideration determination letter”; “The plan will make every effort to resolve the claim payment appeal within 30 calendar days of receipt.” 7.2: non-par “must request a reconsideration of the denial within 65 calendar days from the remittance notification. ... a signed Waiver of Liability Statement must be included.”
rules.applies_to: Anthem MA in KY and IN. Contracted: two-step dispute (mail for GA, IN, KY, MO, OH, WI: ATTN Medicare Payment Dispute Unit, P.O. Box 105187, Atlanta, GA 30348-5187, or Availity); medical-necessity provider appeals within 180 days of the decision letter, 'typically' decided within 60 days. Non-par: payment disputes through the dispute process; appeals of denials 'with member liability' to MCAG, Non-Contracted Provider Appeals, Mailstop OH0205-A537, 4361 Irwin Simpson Rd, Mason, OH 45040.
rules.requires: Upheld reconsideration letters must include 'Support for the action, including applicable statutes, regulations, policies, claims, codes, or provider manual references.'
rules.deadline: Contracted reconsideration 120 days from EOP (target 45-day decision); appeal 30 days (target 30-day decision); med-necessity appeal 180 days (typically 60-day decision). Non-par appeal 65 days.
rules.consequence: Anthem routes non-par 'paid for a different service' disputes to its internal dispute process; CMS guidance 50.1.1 gives non-contracted providers with WOL Subpart M (IRE) rights for downcoding/level of care.
rules.provider_use: Hold Anthem to its own 45/30-day targets in follow-ups and demand the statute/policy support its manual promises. For non-par downcodes, file a WOL reconsideration citing guidance 50.1.1 rather than only the internal dispute.

rules.citation: Wellcare 2026 Medicare Advantage Provider Manual (Internal Approved 04072026), Section 7 'Claims Payment Disputes', 'Non-Participating Provider Reimbursement'; Section 9 'Participating Provider Reconsiderations (Appeals)'
rules.quote: “Providers have 90 calendar days from Wellcare's original utilization management review decision or claim denial to file a Provider appeal.” “Upon receipt of all required documentation, Wellcare has up to 60 calendar days to review the appeal”. “Non-participating Providers are reimbursed at 100% of the Medicare rate in effect on the date of service.”
rules.applies_to: Wellcare (Centene) MA. Claim payment disputes (bundling, untimely filing, unlisted codes) per the provider contract and state QRG; disputes 'received without the necessary documentation will be upheld'.
rules.requires: Complete documentation with the dispute/appeal; reopenings 'at the discretion of Wellcare'.
rules.deadline: Provider appeal: 90 calendar days from the denial; Wellcare decision up to 60 calendar days after complete documentation.
rules.consequence: Untimely appeals denied unless proof of timely filing.
rules.provider_use: Always attach the note and the denial reason documentation on the first submission (Wellcare upholds incomplete disputes). For non-par Wellcare claims, the manual's own '100% of the Medicare rate' statement is a payment floor to cite.

batch_and_channel: Bulk is built in for some routes: UHC's Claims Research Project accepts 20 or more paid or denied claims for the same administrative issue in one online submission (2026 Admin Guide); ALJ requests can aggregate claims with 'similar or related services' to reach the $200 threshold (405.1006(e) via guidance 70.2).

Each MA organization determination is a separate claim decision; no regulation or CMS guidance found addresses one reconsideration letter covering many claims. Safe practice: one cover letter plus a per-claim schedule, each line with claim number, date of service, remittance date, amount at issue and the WOL (for non-contracted).

Waiver of Liability: CMS model form 'Model Waiver of Liability' (ZIP on https://www.cms.gov/medicare/appeals-grievances/managed-care/notices-forms); must be signed by the provider, not the billing agency; e-signature only through a compliant plan portal (guidance 50.1.1).

Fax/mail endpoints from primary pages: Part C IRE (C2C) dismissal reviews: fax (904) 539-4080, phone 1-866-320-0963, P.O. Box 1949 Jacksonville FL 32231-0053. Humana MA non-par appeals: Grievance and Appeal Department, P.O. Box 14165, Lexington, KY 40512-4165; Humana contracted disputes: Availity or Humana Correspondence P.O. Box 14601 Lexington KY 40512. Anthem MA KY/IN contracted disputes: ATTN Medicare Payment Dispute Unit, P.O. Box 105187, Atlanta, GA 30348-5187; Anthem non-par appeals: MCAG Non-Contracted Provider Appeals, Mailstop OH0205-A537, 4361 Irwin Simpson Rd, Mason, OH 45040. UHC non-contracted disputes/reconsiderations: UHC Provider Portal only per its sheet. Wellcare: portal preferred, else address on the member ID card.

Receipt proof drives every federal clock: keep clearinghouse acceptance (999/277CA) for claims and fax confirmations for appeals; reconsiderations count as filed when the plan receives them (422.582(b)(2)).

CMS provider complaint form is an online web form (no special characters such as quotes); one complaint describes one issue but may summarize many claims; optional fields for dates of service and claim number.
Interest math is mechanical and suits automation: paid amount x Treasury rate in effect on the payment date x days late / 365 (FFS method in Pub. 100-04 Ch.1 80.2.2).
does_not_apply: Kentucky and Indiana prompt-pay statutes, their interest rates, and state insurance department claim-payment complaints do not govern MA plans (42 U.S.C. 1395w-26(b)(3); 42 CFR 422.402).

The independent CMS Payment Dispute Resolution Contractor (C2C, 2009 to January 31, 2014) no longer exists; the 2010 PDRC Process Manual is historical. No current MMCM chapter on a PDR process was found.

Subpart M reconsideration, IRE, ALJ and the Star Ratings appeal measures do not apply to a contracted provider's payment denial when the enrollee has no further liability (42 CFR 422.562(c)(2)); those disputes follow the contract.
MA grievance procedures (422.564) are for enrollees only; providers use plan dispute processes and the CMS complaint channels (guidance sec. 30).
Expedited organization determinations and reconsiderations do not cover payment for services already furnished (422.570(a), 422.584(a)).
The ABN (CMS-R-131) may not be used by MA plans or contracted providers (guidance 40.12.1).
The enrollee case-file copy right (guidance 50.5.2) belongs to the enrollee, not to the provider.
No federal day count governs a contracted provider's claim payment or dispute with an MA plan beyond the contract's own prompt-payment clause (422.520(b)).

Under the Original Medicare manual, no interest is paid on full denials or on claims first denied and later paid on appeal; if MA plans follow that convention, interest cannot be claimed on overturned denials (not confirmed for MA).
open_questions: Whether MA plans may apply the Original Medicare interest exceptions (full denials; claims paid after appeal) to 422.520(a)(2) interest: no MA-specific CMS guidance found.
When a plan never issues any remittance or denial for a non-contracted claim, from what date the 65-day reconsideration window runs: not addressed in the regulations or guidance found.

Whether complaints from the new CMS provider complaint form are coded plan-lead category 2.70 and counted in Star Ratings C27: the CTM SOP was read only from a third-party copy, and the Dec. 2025 memo says CMS triages first.
Which MA plans and products (HMO vs PPO vs D-SNP) the practice actually holds written contracts with; this decides which rules apply to each claim.
Whether any Humana, Anthem, UHC or Wellcare D-SNP in KY or IN is an 'applicable integrated plan' (integrated appeals, 30-day reconsideration clock).
Whether plans will accept one reconsideration covering many claims; regulations and guidance are silent.

Whether E/M or Mohs code-level downcoding by a plan's claim-editing software counts as a medical-necessity/level-of-care organization determination requiring 422.566(d) physician review in every case; the CMS FAQ treats refusals to pay 'the type or level of services' as organization determinations, but code-editing policy is not addressed directly.
Exact Part C IRE contract deadlines: 422.592(b) defers to the CMS contract; the 60-day payment timeframe comes from CMS's IRE web page, not the regulation.

The CMS appeals guidance PDF (effective July 6, 2026) carries a footer saying it is not releasable to the public, although CMS links it publicly from its managed care appeals pages; its text was used as published.
The Star Ratings financial effect (quality bonus payments, rebates) was not researched here; only the measure definitions and weights were verified.
